text:
ana: Quick sync — final safety-net readiness for the Routing & Cost Controls launch. I want a quick pass on the minimum GA checklist so we can ship next week. High level: SLA, docs, oncall, monitoring, pricing, rollback/fallbacks.

kevin: Working through perf smoke today. Can we lock the SLA targets? Last draft was 99.9% availability and p95 latency <= 180ms for standard tier. Is that still the goal?

ana: @kevin yes, PM confirmation — 99.9 / p95 180ms standard, p95 120ms premium. Add a degraded-mode SLA of 99.0 when fallback is in use.

priya: Noted. For degraded-mode SLA we need explicit automated fallback detection + alerting. I'll add an incident rule: if fallback rate > 5% for 5m -> P1. Is that acceptable?

kevin: 5% threshold sounds reasonable. We'll add telemetry: route_match, fallback_reason, latency_bucket in resume.

miguel: On pricing readiness: need final per-token cost calc with expected batching savings. Can eng provide a delta between current and optimized profiles? I need that by EOD Friday for the pricing page.

kevin: I'll push numbers from the Optimize runbook. Expect ~18-22% unit cost reduction with caching + adaptive batching for typical chat workloads. I'll put a summary in the release PR.

sara: Docs: I need owners for the runbook, quickstart, migration guide, and change log. Prefer a single page called "operational-safety" that links to runbooks and SLOs. Who owns each?

kevin: I'll own the runbook + migration steps for existing routes.

ana: Sara owns the public quickstart + pricing blurb. Miguel can review pricing wording. Priya, can you own the internal oncall runbook/alert flows?

priya: I can own the oncall runbook. Will add playbook steps and the escalation path to eng-oncall. Also need a preflight smoke test (see snippet below) that runs on deploy.

priya: ```sh
# preflight smoke
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" 
  -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":16}' 
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
# assert 200 and latency < 500ms
```

sara: Nice. I'll link that in docs and add a one-liner for customers about expected latency bands and degraded-mode behavior.

ana: Support model: small initial SLA-based ticket queue managed by Support L2 + Eng oncall for 72hrs post-GA. After that handback to normal SLA routing. Agree?

miguel: Financial guardrail: set a burst cap for new customers to avoid runaway billing. We have a template in finops-billing. I'll add recommended default caps and an escalation to sales for limits removal.

kevin: Rollout plan note: canary at 5% traffic for 24h, then 25% for 12h if no critical. We need manual signoff after 25% before full. Also automatic fallback to baseline model on errors >1% for 10m.

ana: Can someone add a one-paragraph blurb for the launch announcement that clarifies availability across Hosted/Dedicated/Private and the SLA differences? Sara + Miguel?

sara: I'll draft the blurb and post in #announcements for copy review. Miguel will confirm pricing lines.

oncall-bot: Reminder: Oncall rotation next week starts Mon 09:00 UTC — Priya assigned as primary for the first 72h post-launch.

priya: Got it. I'll schedule a 30m handoff meeting with Eng oncall tomorrow to walkthrough playbook.

ana: Outstanding blockers: (1) Runbook link in Console, (2) pricing copy + finops caps, (3) automated smoke in CI, (4) final SLA doc in Confluence. Owners: kevin, miguel, priya, sara. Can we close all by EOD Friday?

kevin: Runbook PR out in 3h.

miguel: Pricing copy will land in draft tonight.

sara: Docs draft will be ready for review by Thursday afternoon.

priya: Smoke test integrated into release pipeline by Friday morning.

ana: Great. If all owners confirm green by Friday we mark GA-ready and schedule the 5% canary for next Mon 02:00 UTC.

kevin: 👍

miguel: :+1:

sara: :rocket:

priya: 👍 I'll post the oncall playbook link when done.

ana: Thanks all — small checklist in the PR to track these final items. If anything slips, flag here and we decide scope vs date.
